Thousands of Private Attorney-Inmate Phone Conversations in 37 States Recorded and Stored by Prison Phone Firm

massive computer hack of prison phone records has revealed inmates across the country have had their calls with attorneys recorded, potentially violating their legal and constitutional rights.

The investigative website The Intercept obtained records of 70 million phone calls placed by prisoners in 37 states, following a “major breach of security” at Securus Technologies, which contracts with prisons and jails to provide phone services.

Records of the calls, which took place between December 2011 and spring of 2014, were leaked to The Intercept by an anonymous hacker who claims Securus has violated the constitutional rights of inmates.

“Particularly notable within the vast trove of phone records are what appear to be at least 14,000 recorded conversations between inmates and attorneys, a strong indication that at least some of the recordings are likely confidential and privileged legal communications — calls that never should have been recorded in the first place,” Jordan Smith and Micah Lee reported at The Intercept.

David Fathi, director of the ACLU National Prison Project, said the recordings “may be the most massive breach of the attorney-client privilege in modern U.S. history, and that’s certainly something to be concerned about.

“A lot of prisoner rights are limited because of their conviction and incarceration, but their protection by the attorney-client privilege is not,” Fathi said.

In addition to possibly violating inmates’ rights, Securus’ phone systems, which it claims are secure, have been proven not to be.

“We will provide the most technologically advanced audio and video communications platform to allow calls with a high level of security,” reads the company’s Integrity Pledge, according to The Intercept. “We understand that confidentiality of calls is critical, and we will follow all Federal, State, and Local laws in the conduct of our business.”

The company was sued last year by Austin, Texas, attorneys who claim their calls with clients over Securus’ phone system have been recorded and leaked to prosecutors. “How do you plan your strategy?” defense attorney Scott Smith asked. “It’s like being at the Super Bowl and one team gets to put a microphone in the huddle of another team.”

I recently started playing Elite Dangerous. This led to me looking a a HOTAS which led to me looking up other games that were compatible with the ones I was looking at. I mean, If I am considering dropping $200 on a gaming peripheral, I want to know what games I can use it with.

Anyway, one of the games listed for the HOTAS I am looking at was DCS. I had never heard of this game before, but I like the idea of flying an A-10 or a Spitfire so I started digging into it. The concept of a modular game sounds really cool. Like RTS, Used the Command Map module, Like to fly? Choose your plane or Helicopter. Want to drive a tank? Get the plugin for that.

My question is...How does it actually play? How is the community? Is it a good game or is there a reason I haven't heard about it. Also, how it it for single player? Are there canned missions? What is the learning curve like?
Anyone here Play DCS? If so, How it it?

DCS world comes with a free SU-25. It doesn't have a fully interactive cockpit buy it'll give you a good idea whether you'll like the game or not. I really enjoy flying the A-10c. It took a few days to get introduced to all the systems. There are lots of YouTube videos on how to fly, and the dcs forum is pretty active, though it's mostly drooling over the upcoming f-15 dlc. I personally can't stand flying any other flight simulation after getting accustom to the complicated controls.

Actually, it also comes with the mustang trainer with a full interactive cockpit to give you a much better idea what to expect from the more detailed modules with interactive cockpits.

Trying to wing it and figure out how to start the Mustang without any instruction was fun and hilarious for me and helped sell me on the game. Basically if I can't even figure out how to start the damn thing I know this is the sim for me.

DCS has a great community! Here's a small taste of the game play

The module aspect of the DCS is nice. Some of them are basic (they look and act like what they're supposed to be, but not in-depth), and a few are very detailed and in-depth. The A10 and Blackshark are basically their flagship products. There are lots of single player missions you can download. They're user made so their quality varies, but the good ones are really good.

Multiplayer is great too when you find someone to fly with. You'll need teamspeak or something like that to get the most out of it. Speaking of which, you'd better have trackir or something similar too.

You say you never heard of it... probably because it's a really niche community, but flightsim community is actually pretty big once you dig into it. We (supposedly) have /v/flightsim here too but it's a ghost town :o

As for learning it, there are plenty of resources thanks to the big community. But, if you want the A10, you're going to have to invest a lot of time into it before you feel like you're having fun blowing things up. You can try the simpler, smaller module to get a taste of the DCS world.

Let me know if you have any other questions! If you're just discovering DCS then you're in for a treat!

Awesome, that is what I wanted to hear. I Love flight sim games and I have had a woeful absence of them for the last 15 years. I used to almost exclusively play Flight Sim 98, Janes F-15 and Wing Commander, along with a great old Mech Sim called G-Nome (would love to find a decent, modern Mech sim). Picking up Elite Dangerous has rekindled my love for them. I want to make sure there are enough to justify purchasing the X55 Rhino.

I grew up with those too! The golden age of flight sim, where they would be a new release every few years, on almost any plane you can imagine.

The flight sim renaissance is happening and they're slowly coming back. There are a number of choices for both military and civilian sims now.

One last piece of advice. Watch out for your wallet in DCS. It ended up smashing my bank account pretty hard in peripherals and modules when all was said and done. And all isn't said and done yet because the MFG crosswinds I ordered are going to be shipping in the next two weeks.

Also I'm really feeling like I need a bank of 3 way toggle switches on my home made toggle panel for it.

It's pretty fun. I find it's strength is in the blisteringly complex modules like A-10c and Black Shark 2. I prefer the aspect of slowly learning a very realistic sim to the watered down simplistic modules like the SU-25T it comes with and the Flaming Cliffs modules.

The FC3 craft can still be fun though too. Multiplayer seems like it's pretty much nothing but F15C online though. Because the F15C is leaps and bounds above all the other planes and basically annihilates everything else with aim-120 missiles. The WW2 servers and planes are probably a different story of course, I have yet to get into them, but I could see those being more fun online.

I find the game is kind of in a state of flux right now. The stable version 1.2.whatever is out and playable. But the 1.5 open beta is also out, and while it's mostly broken as fuck as you'd expect of a beta, the graphics and speed improvement is so much it hurts to go back to playing 1.2.

The learning curve is pretty mild for the easy planes like the SU-25, to blisteringly hard for the full detail modules like the A10-C. Also, I recommend having trackir, I do, and I couldn't live without it.

The community varies by module as far as I can see. As you might expect, the easy access modules have more clowns and the serious sim modules tend to better.
